What does strike options out is which subshells are available after [Xe]: 5s is already full inside the [Xe] core, which removes option 4, and 6d lies above both 6s and 5d so it cannot be occupied while 5d is empty, which removes option 3 - leaving only options 1 and 2 to decide between.

ratings.concept: Acidic buffer: a weak acid together with the salt of that acid; a strong acid and its salt cannot buffer because the acid is fully ionised
ratings.strategy_evidence: HClO4 is the only strong acid among the four acids printed; since buffering needs a weak acid, that single fact strikes out options 1, 2 and 4 together and settles the answer on option 3.

traps.label: true_statement_trap

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: the task is negated; H3PO4 with Na3PO4 is again a weak acid with a salt of the same acid, and the mixture buffers once proton transfer has set up the H2PO4-/HPO4(2-) pair, so this too answers the un-negated question

traps.label: true_statement_trap

It is recorded as a true_statement_trap on the same ground as options 1 and 4; the key stands on HClO4 being the only strong acid, which is not in doubt.

ratings.concept: Conductivity of aqueous solutions follows the degree of ionisation: strong electrolyte > weak electrolyte > non-electrolyte
ratings.strategy_evidence: HCl is the only strong electrolyte printed; since conductance is carried by ions and only a strong electrolyte is fully ionised, that one fact strikes out options 1, 2 and 3 at once.

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: fructose is a molecular sugar that dissolves without ionising at all, so its solution carries no ions beyond those of water itself; its conductance is the lowest of the four and no route makes it the highest

ratings.reason: This question requires applying the ionisation criterion to four named solutes, demonstrated by option 4's "Hydrochloric acid, HCl", the only one of the four that is completely ionised in water.
ratings.note: Options 1 and 3 are left untagged. Ammonia and acetic acid are weak electrolytes that do conduct, just less than HCl, so they are not wrong on a nameable mistake - they are correctly ranked below the key - and no wrong operation turns either into the best conductor. Tagging them would mean asserting a preference rather than a route.

group_note: All six were read as the same printed shape - one question, four answers, no lettered block or printed list - and q003 is the member that sits least comfortably with the rest, since its stem prints two thermochemical equations with values and so is data-bearing where the other five are not. Three stated rules kept the group consistent. (1) DEMAND: four members are `application` - a stated rule (the filling rules, valence and connectivity, the K-scaling rule, the buffer criterion, the ionisation criterion) applied to the case the stem prints. q003 alone is `explanatory_reasoning`, and the test for that is in its own stem: the fact is conceded ("the process ... is unfavourable") and only the causal link remains, whereas in the other five the fact itself is at issue. No member is `recall`: in each of the five, the rule has to be applied to a species or a stoichiometry not given in the books, and under the rebuilt definition applying a rule still requires knowing it. (2) STRUCTURE: `several_independent_checks` where each option or each candidate is adjudicated separately and the verdicts combined (q002 four configurations, q004 four candidate structures enumerated, q006 four pairs, q007 four solutes); `single_step` where one relation or one judgement settles it (q003, q005). Nothing in this packet is multi_step_dependent: no member requires one computed result to be carried into a later step, and four option-checks are not four steps. (3) TRAPS: tagged only where the option and the route can both be named. The two negated questions differ from the rest exactly as their polarity requires - q006's three distractors are all genuine acidic buffers, so each carries `true_statement_trap` with the polarity quoted, while q007, which is not negated, has only one option with a nameable route and so carries one trap. q002's option set is the clearest case of a grid rather than a spread: all four options total ten electrons beyond [Xe], so the count eliminates nothing and the subshell availability has to do the work, which is why the elimination evidence here names what does NOT strike options out as well as what does; its two unreachable options carry `no_derivation_route` with the demonstration given in each route (6d above 6s, 5s inside the core) and never as an assertion. Where no route exists, no label is forced: q007's weak electrolytes are untagged and said to be so in the note. No trap sits on any official answer.
